question: Explain when a two-sided limit lim_{x->c} f(x) exists.
student_answer: It exists if the right-hand limit exists as x approaches c from the positive side.

chunks.text: Theorem: The two-sided limit lim_{x->c} f(x) = L exists if and only if both one-sided limits exist and are equal: lim_{x->c^-} f(x) = lim_{x->c^+} f(x) = L.
